subject: SIEM routing & egress questions for private deployment
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: sec-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIEM routing & egress questions for private deployment

Hi Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We have a few follow-ups from our security and cloud networking teams before we kick off the POC for the private VPC deployment. High level asks below — please point us to the recommended patterns and any sample configs you can share.

1) Export mode: what are the supported options for sending logs/metrics/traces from a Redwood private deployment in our VPC into our Splunk Cloud (HEC)? Specifically: centralized forwarder (customer-managed), sidecar agent per instance, or push directly from the runtime?

2) Egress & firewall: list of outbound IPs/ports we need to allow (HEC endpoints, certificate revocation, telemetry endpoints). Do you support configuring a single egress CIDR or do we need to allow many ephemeral IPs?

3) Auth & encryption: does Redwood support mutual TLS for the forwarder to HEC? How do you recommend handling token rotation and secret management for HEC tokens?

4) Tracing hooks: we want span-level visibility mapped to our traces (Jaeger). What instrumentation do you expose and how are trace ids correlated with request logs?

5) Audit artifacts: we will need a sample evidence bundle for SOC review (list of logs, retention configuration, and change history hooks). Any existing template?

I've attached our SIEM requirements doc (acme-siem-requirements-v2.pdf) and a rough diagram of our VPC. Let us know if you prefer a call.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Head of Cloud Security — AcmeHealth

Attachment: acme-siem-requirements-v2.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM routing & egress questions for private deployment

Hi Alice — great questions, thanks for the doc. Summary response and a recommended POC configuration below; attaching a brief options doc (redwood-private-siem-options.md) and a sample network diagram.

Short answers:
- Supported export modes: 1) customer-managed centralized forwarder deployed in your VPC (recommended for Splunk Cloud/HEC), 2) per-node sidecar agent (lower blast radius), 3) direct push from runtime to HEC (supported but requires careful token mgmt and is less common).
- Egress: you can lock to a small set of outbound endpoints if you run the centralized forwarder — the forwarder is the only component that needs network egress to Splunk HEC. If you choose direct push, each instance will require egress.
- Auth: we support HEC token-based auth and can do mutual TLS for customers that require client certs. Token rotation is handled via integration with your KMS and can be automated by the forwarder (we provide scripts).
- Tracing: Redwood emits OpenTelemetry spans; the forwarder can attach trace_id to log events (field: trace.parent_id) so SIEM correlation is straightforward. We also export Jaeger-format spans if you prefer.
- Evidence: attached is a template of logs and retention configuration we typically supply for SOC reviews.

Recommended POC (our suggested start):
1) Deploy a single centralized forwarder in your telemetry subnet. Forwarder config: Splunk HEC (443), TLS with server validation, optional mTLS.
2) Allow egress from forwarder to Splunk HEC IPs (we'll provide a minimal set). Runtime instances talk to forwarder on internal port 24224 (TLS).
3) Enable OpenTelemetry on the runtime; set the forwarder as the OTLP endpoint and enable trace_id enrichment on logs.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) will send the small collector config and the minimal egress CIDR list. Can we schedule a 30-min network alignment early next week?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-siem-options.md, proposed-network-diagram.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM routing & egress questions for private deployment

Alice — adding a few low-level details and a sample HEC configuration you can drop into your forwarder. I also included a small checklist for the networking team.

Network checklist (centralized forwarder model):
- Outbound: TCP 443 to your Splunk HEC ingestion URL (we recommend using the FQDN, then allow the resolved IPs on your firewall if you cannot egress to FQDNs).
- Inbound (internal): TCP 24224 (TLS) from Redwood runtime instances to forwarder. Enforce mTLS on this port if you require strong auth between runtime and forwarder.
- DNS: ensure forwarder can resolve HEC hostnames and CRL/OCSP endpoints.
- NAT/EIP: If your firewall requires static egress IPs, deploy the forwarder in a nat'ed subnet with an Elastic IP.

Sample Splunk HEC stanza (forwarder config - template):
HEC_ENDPOINT=https://input-us1.splunkcloud.com:443
HEC_TOKEN=<<REDACTED_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER>>
TLS_VERIFY=true
CLIENT_CERT=/etc/forwarder/certs/client.pem  # optional for mTLS

Token rotation: use the forwarder's credential provider to pull tokens from your KMS. We support AWS Secrets Manager / HashiVault (examples in the attached doc).

Tracing: enable OTLP gRPC export from the runtime to the forwarder (port 4317). The forwarder will create and emit a combined event that includes span.trace_id and span.span_id fields. In Splunk, create a field extraction on trace_id to stitch logs/traces together.

Evidence bundle: we'll prepare an evidence zip with the following artifacts: forwarder config, runtime OTLP config, sample logs with trace_id, change history for forwarder deployment, and an egress ACL excerpt. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.

One open item: Alice — can you confirm if your Splunk tenancy requires IP allowlisting (static IP) or if DNS/FQDN-based egress is acceptable? If IP allowlisting is required we will send exact EIP recommendations and guidance on high-availability NAT.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: sample-forwarder-config.yaml
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM routing & egress questions for private deployment

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is perfect. We do require IP allowlisting for ingestion (Splunk policy), so we will need the static EIP guidance and an HA NAT pattern. Please include the minimal IP set and an estimate for the number of EIPs needed for an HA forwarder pair.

We are happy to run the suggested POC next week. Can you send a calendar invite for Wed 2028-04-25 10:00 AM PDT for network alignment + handoff? Also, please include the evidence bundle when it's ready.

Regards,
Alice
